hints: Focus on the Hess cycle link between formation and combustion, products minus reactants is the key idea.
Count the moles carefully from the equation, you make 3 moles of $\text{CO}_2$ and 4 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ from 1 mole of propan-1-ol.
Remember to keep the negative signs and subtract the reactant, subtracting a negative value turns into adding its positive value.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Hess law rule**

Think of forming everything from elements first. The shortcut is always products minus reactants.

$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{reactants})$$

**Write out products and reactants**

Products are $3\text{CO}_2(g) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. Reactants are $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}(l) + 4\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g)$.

Remember $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ of $\text{O}_2(g)$ is zero because it is an element in its standard state.

**Substitute with correct multipliers**

Now put the numbers in, keeping the minus signs with them.

$$\Delta H_c^\ominus = [3(-394) + 4(-286)] - [(-303) + 0]$$

**Rearrange to match the options**

Simplify the double negative. Minus negative 303 becomes plus 303.

$$\Delta H_c^\ominus = -3(394) - 4(286) + 303$$

That is the same as $303 - (4 \times 286) - (3 \times 394)$, a large negative value as expected for combustion.

options.A: Incorrect. This forgets the stoichiometry, it uses only 1 mole each of $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ instead of 3 and 4. It also mishandles the subtraction of the reactant.
options.B: Correct. This is $[3 \times (-394) + 4 \times (-286)] - (-303)$ rearranged. The products term is negative and large, minus the negative reactant gives $+303$, so $303 - (4 \times 286) - (3 \times 394)$.
options.C: Incorrect. This uses positive magnitudes for formation enthalpies and ignores the 3 and 4 multipliers. Formation values must stay negative because forming $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is exothermic.
options.D: Incorrect. This adds all the magnitudes together as positive numbers. Combustion must be strongly exothermic (negative), and Hess law requires products minus reactants, not plus.
